Header: Pseudoperonospora cubensis Bangla name: Kumra fasoler ‘Chata rog’

Prevention: Select land with good air movement and without shading to minimize leaf wetness.
Avoid dense planting for good aeration and exposure to sunlight.
Remove volunteer/wild cucurbit plants in and around the cucurbit field.
Fallow crop rotation with non- cucurbit crops (such as maize) at 1-year intervals.
Use balanced fertilizers to keep plant growth vigorous.
Avoid overhead irrigation to prevent leaf wetness.
Monitoring: Visit the field regularly and examine cucurbit plants from the vegetative to fruiting stages.
Downy mildew infects all cucurbits, but cucumber, sponge gourd and ridge gourd are more sensitive to diseases.
Disease becomes more aggressive when heavy dews, fog or frequent rains occur.
Initially, small pale areas appear on upper surface of lower leaves which change to yellow angular spots restricted by veins.
Under surface of infected area of leaves appears water-soaked and fungus growth (mould) may be observed.
The entire leaf may die quickly.
